# tailess

> Write Tailwind classes as a typed object grouped by breakpoint and state. A build
> plugin enumerates every class the runtime can build and hands the list to Tailwind, so
> the classes actually get CSS.

## The one rule

**Every class must be a literal at the call site.**

The runtime builds `md:p-6` while the page renders. Tailwind never sees that string in
the source, so a build plugin predicts it from the call site and safelists it. When the
prediction is impossible, the class still lands on the element and **no rule is ever
generated** — no console error, no build error, nothing. The element is simply unstyled.

This is the opposite of several habits that are normally good:

```ts
// ❌ every one of these is silently unstyled
const size = "p-4";
ss({ md: size });                     // a variable
ss({ md: `text-${scale}` });          // an interpolated template
ss({ ...spread });                    // a spread
ss({ [key]: "grid" });                // a computed key
withPrefix(dynamicPrefix, "p-4");     // a computed prefix
import { ss as tw } from "tailess";   // a renamed import — kills the whole file

// ✅ keep the class literal, move the choice
ss({ md: "p-4" });
match(size, { sm: "p-2", lg: "p-8" });          // a lookup, all branches literal
ss({ md: cond ? "p-4" : "p-2" });               // both branches are read
ss({ base: "w-[var(--w)]" });                   // a value from data goes in a CSS var
style={vars({ "--w": `${percent}%` })}
```

`base` is the exception: it adds no prefix, so its value passes through and Tailwind
finds the literal wherever it really lives.

## API

- `ss(...)` — the whole `className` in one call. Keys are `base`, breakpoints (`sm`…`2xl`),
  `max-*` ranges, container queries (`@md`, `@max-md`), and states (`hover`, `dark`,
  `group-hover`, `peer-checked`, `has-focus`, `not-first`, …). 305 keys, closed union.
- `cn(...)` — join + `tailwind-merge`, nothing else.
- `responsive`, `on`, `until`, `between`, `data`, `aria`, `match`, `withPrefix`
- `supports` / `notSupports` — feature queries. Negation is only ever `not-supports-*`.
- `group` / `peer` / `container` — named variants.
- `has` / `notHas` / `inside`, `nth` / `nthLast` / `nthOfType` / `nthLastOfType`
- `variants(...)` — component recipes, with `slots`, `extend`, boolean variants and
  compound rules. Accepts `cva`'s call shape and key names.
- `vars(...)` — CSS custom properties for values a class cannot carry.
- `configure({ merge, onWarn, keys })`

Nesting runs one way: a helper goes **inside** an `ss` bucket, never the reverse.
`ss({ md: on("hover", "underline") })` is right — `"md:hover:underline"`; the bucket key
and the helper each add their own variant, so do not repeat one in the other.
`on("hover", { base: … })` builds the class `hover:base`.

## Checking

```bash
npx tailess doctor   # is the plugin wired up at all?
npx tailess check    # compile for real; exits 1 if a class has no rule
```

The build plugin reports ten things it can prove wrong from the source. Of the shapes
above it reports the variable, the interpolated template and the renamed import — and
**not** the spread, the computed key or the computed prefix: for those the scanner
enumerates nothing, so there is no candidate for `check` to compile and it exits 0. A
green `tailess check` does not prove those three are styled. Do not write them.

The checks only speak about a file that imports from `"tailess"`. Reach the helpers
through your own re-export and the classes are still enumerated and still verified by
`check`, but the source-level warnings go quiet.
